How the calculators work

Each calculator starts from a proven basic design and works out the individual parts from it. Section, length and quantity give the volume of timber in cubic metres. Multiply by the price per m³, add an allowance for waste, and you have the cost estimate.

Sections are shown in millimetres, as timber merchants in the UK, Ireland and Australia sell them. The calculators use continental standard sizes such as 120 × 120 mm posts. If your merchant does not stock a size, pick the next stock size up, for example 150 × 150 mm instead of 140 × 140 mm.

You can change the timber price in every calculator, for example to match a quote from your merchant. The example prices are retail prices including VAT or GST, in pounds for the UK, euros for Ireland and Australian dollars for Australia. The currency is picked from your location, and you can switch it under every calculator.

All timber sections are guide values and do not replace a structural calculation. Carports and patio covers may need planning permission and building regulations approval, and a structural engineer's check depending on where you live.
